_comment: Upstream-owned files this fork intentionally changes. Anything not listed here fails scripts/check-fork-surface.mjs; the fix is to move the change into one of our own trees, or to add it here deliberately. Budgets are the most this fork may change in one commit — they catch creep, not a single honest edit. maxNetLines is the most one commit may change; maxTotalLines is the most this fork may have changed in total. A note the per-file entries cannot carry: this fork keeps `screenshots/` entirely local (see `.gitignore`), which deletes 12 images upstream tracks (`PAP-*.png`, `PR-*.png`). At a merge, keep the rule and drop upstream's images again rather than restoring them.

entries.reason: Tailwind v4 @source directive for plugin bundles. Plugin UI ships no stylesheet and is styled by the host's compiled Tailwind, and v4 only auto-detects sources under ui/, so without this every utility a plugin invents is silently missing. Cannot live elsewhere: the directive is only read from the CSS entry.
Page-slot layout option (full-height), so a plugin page can opt out of the host's default scroll container.
Validator half of the page-slot layout option above.
Test for the page-slot layout option above.
Honour the page-slot layout option when rendering a plugin page.
Entry points for the repo gates (test:defenses and friends). A gate nobody can run is not a gate.

Points at this fork's own conventions (docs-coolie/*, .agents/skills, doc/plans). AGENTS.md is the one file every AGENTS.md-reading tool loads, so the pointers cannot live in our own tree; they are written as plain paths rather than @imports, because an import is inlined into the system prompt on every request and would be paid on every turn.

This manifest itself, and entirely ours — it does not exist upstream. It sits under scripts/ only because that is where the gate is wired (package.json and check-testing-defenses.mjs call it), and that path prefix is the only reason the gate asks about it. The budget is loose on purpose: the file grows by one entry per upstream file we intentionally change, and that growth is the file working, not creep. Raised from 360 when the ontology-spec workflow and the DSH/coolie-native adapters were declared in one batch.

Marker block for the ICP filing footer, plus lang="zh-CN" for a zh-CN deployment. Markers only — the block stays empty unless an operator configures a filing, so upstream behaviour is unchanged without one. The injection lives on the server because the filing number is deployment config and must not be baked into a UI build.

Serves the optional public landing page at `/` in static mode. It has to be here rather than in our own tree because this file is what owns route order: `/` is claimed before the SPA fallback registers, and `/index.html` and every other route keep returning the app shell. Off unless PAPERCLIP_LANDING_ENABLED is set.

Fills the ICP footer marker block. This file already owns the one other place the server rewrites its own index.html (favicon and runtime branding), and the escaping helper it used to keep privately now comes from server/src/html-escape.ts so the footer and landing page share one implementation.

New file: resolves and renders the ICP/公安 filing footer. No upstream counterpart, so there is nothing to reconcile at a merge. Its own tree by origin, but it must sit beside the two callers (ui-branding and landing-page) rather than in a package of its own.
New file: the HTML escaping shared by the injected footer and the landing page. No upstream counterpart. Three callers is why it is a module rather than a copy.

New file: the public landing page. No upstream counterpart. The line count is dominated by two things that are content rather than logic — the built-in catalogue of what this deployment has built, and the inline stylesheet — which is also why the operator can override the catalogue from a JSON file without a rebuild.
New file: tests for the filing footer, including the escaping of a filing number. No upstream counterpart.
New file: tests for the landing page — the enable switch, the catalogue override and its fallbacks, and the refusal to link anything but http(s). No upstream counterpart.

Covers the filing footer reaching the app shell, and staying out of it when no filing is configured. Added here rather than in a new file because this suite already owns the SPA fallback HTML that the footer is injected into.

Reads PAPERCLIP_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL into Config.bootstrapAdminEmail. Env-only rather than also a paperclip.json key: the pin is a property of the deployment an operator sets once, and a file-config key would mean touching the config schema that the CLI and shared packages also compile against.

Two databaseHooks that call the pinned-email bootstrap on user create and on session create. This is the only place that sees a credential sign-up and sign-in as they happen, and it is added conditionally, so an instance without the pin keeps upstream's options object byte for byte.

New file: decides whether a sign-up or sign-in should grant the first instance admin, and reuses server/src/first-admin-claim.ts for the locked, once-only insert rather than writing a second claim path. No upstream counterpart.

New file: the matching rules, the config parse, and the claim outcomes against a real Postgres (including the negative case — an address the operator did not pin never gets admin). No upstream counterpart.

New file: drives the real Better Auth mount so the hooks are proven to fire on sign-up and on sign-in. The sign-in case is the one operators hit (register first, pin after), and it is the only coverage of the session hook's email lookup. No upstream counterpart.

Names the environment variable the pending page tells an operator to set, next to the CLI fallback it already exported. One source for both, so the page cannot drift from the variable the server reads.

The public-instance branch used to offer the host CLI as the way to finish setup, which is not a path a product can ask a customer to take. It now leads with the pinned email, and splits on whether a session already exists: signed out it offers sign-in, signed in it can only offer a sign-out, because `AuthPage` bounces any session-bearing request back to `/` and the grant fires when a session is created. The budget covers both halves of that branch, since they are one screen and one decision.

The design-lab fixture keeps its own copy of the pending screens; leaving it on the old wording, or missing the public-signed-in state, would make the lab document a design the app no longer ships. Fixture copy is most of the growth here, which is the point of the file.

Adds `retry: false` to the pre-auth experimental-settings read. The default backoff left the shell's loading gate closed for seconds after a 401/403 and hit the endpoint four times before giving up; the resolver already fails open, so a single attempt is the correct behaviour. Cannot live elsewhere: this hook is the only reader and it owns the query options.

Adds an `enabled` option so the globally-mounted onboarding wizard can hold the protected adapter listing until it is actually open. Matches the sibling useDisabledAdaptersSync/useAdapterRegistryLoaded lookups; without it a signed-out visitor fetches /api/adapters on every route. The default keeps every other caller unchanged.
Passes `enabled: effectiveOnboardingOpen` to the capability lookup above, exactly as its two sibling global lookups already do. One call site plus the comment saying why.

Replaces the `canSubmit` boolean with `validateCredentials`, so a submit either sends or shows the first reason it did not. The button carried `aria-disabled` while staying clickable and the native `required` attributes meant the JS error branch was unreachable; the form is now `noValidate` and JSDOM-safe. Also adds the email shape check that `type="email"` was assumed to provide.

Covers `validateCredentials`: the accept cases plus the missing-email, malformed-email, missing-password and short-sign-up-password messages, which is the behaviour that replaced the unreachable 'Please fill in all required fields.' branch.

The public bootstrap-pending coverage: the old case asserted the defect (it passed a session and expected 'Sign in / Create account'), so it became two — signed out keeps the sign-in offer, signed in gets the sign-out — plus the assertions that each state does not render the other's affordance. Also supplies `useNavigate` in the router mock, now that the no-organization screen routes to an invite.

Wires useSignOut into the pending screen, and gives the no-organization screen a way forward: it accepts an invite link or code and routes to /invite/:token, so a signed-in account with no membership is no longer a copy-only dead end. The budget covers the invite form, the exported token parser, and the sign-out wiring.

New file: unit coverage for `inviteTokenFromInput` — a raw code, a full invite URL, a trailing slash, a query string, a fragment, surrounding whitespace, and blank input. No upstream counterpart, so nothing to reconcile at a merge.
Expand dashboard service with cockpit efficiency metrics: lead time distribution, task progress & failure rate, agent idle duration, workshop throughput, and budget vs monthly spend telemetry.
Expose GET /api/companies/:companyId/metrics/cockpit returning dedicated cockpit metrics bundle.
Unit tests covering cockpit efficiency metrics: quota, progress, idle, deliveryCycle, efficiency, and failureRate.
Forwarder script for mobile Expo app OTA publishing, delegating to clients/expo/scripts/publish-ota.sh to export and sync bundles to tc-coolie-claw.

Forwarder script for Coolie Web (clients/expo-paperclip-web) OTA publishing, the paperclip-web sibling of scripts/publish-ota.sh. Sits under scripts/ only because that is where the OTA entry points are wired; the payload itself lives in clients/, which we own. Needed because the two apps publish to different OTA roots (/ota vs /ota/paperclip-web) and one forwarder cannot serve both.

Fork ships ontology and workspace-diff plugins as self-hosted auto-installs so the mobile cockpit's ontology/code-review tabs work out of the box, and makes the deprecated chat bundle opt-in: `resolveSelfHostedAutoInstallKeys` drops the `chat` key unless `COOLIE_USE_PLUGIN_CHAT=true`, because ChatHome (server `board-chat` + the clients' `board-inline` surface) replaces plugin-chat. The catalog entry for `chat` points at `_deprecated/plugin-chat` so the opt-in still resolves where that leftover bundle exists.

Upstream's test asserted the self-hosted auto-install list is exactly `["kubernetes"]`. This fork adds ontology and workspace-diff (see the bundled-plugins.ts entry above), so that assertion cannot hold; it now asserts the boot default keeps kubernetes/ontology/workspace-diff and drops chat unless opted in. Read together with the bundled-plugins.ts entry: it pins the same divergence from the other side.

Board chat runs on `hermes` (the operator's own agent) instead of `claude`, and its deployment gate admits `authenticated` as well as `local_trusted`, because this fork's install is single-operator (one boss) rather than an upstream multi-tenant deployment. Registered so the next upstream merge resolves this file by intent: keep upstream's relay logic, re-apply the hermes spawn and the widened gate.

Upstream's version of this test asserted `authenticated` is refused. This fork allows it, and `DEPLOYMENT_MODES` holds only `local_trusted` and `authenticated`, so that assertion cannot hold: rewritten to assert `authenticated` is admitted, with the refusal branch kept for a mode outside today's union. Its correctness depends on the board-chat.ts entry above, so the two are read together.

Fork-specific ignores: the mobile client tree (`clients/`), the Expo/OTA and coolie-claw deploy outputs, local crash dumps and CLI logs (`core`, `coscli*`), Command Code's local-only state, and test/exploration screenshots, which this fork keeps local rather than committing. A recurring divergence by nature — every new local artifact kind adds a line — so it is declared rather than reduced.

Carries the fork's DS-style ontology spec card: a `建域 xxx` prompt plans an ontology domain, and the card renders that spec (object types, relation types, modelling problems) with its approval status without offering an apply button, because the server writes the model only after a human approves the spec. It is appended into upstream's own message list and reuses upstream's trigger detection, which is why it cannot be a component in our own tree. One commit, 114 lines added, nothing removed: at a merge, keep upstream's render path and re-append the card.

Fork release script, and entirely ours: upstream ships no release-app.sh, so there is nothing to reconcile at a merge. It sits under scripts/ only because that is where the release entry points are wired, and that path prefix is the only reason the gate asks about it. Content is pre-flight and sanity checks, version.json read permissions, runtimeVersion single-sourced for OTA, and the rule that every release must correspond to a commit — the last paired with backfill-commit-sha.sh below.

Fork script: builds the h5 client and rsyncs its dist to the deployment's web root. No upstream counterpart — upstream has no clients/ to publish — so nothing to reconcile at a merge, and it cannot live in a package of its own for the same reason. Same shape and same reason as the two publish-ota forwarders above.

Fork script: backfills the commit SHA a release records. It exists as the repair path for the rule release-app.sh enforces, so the two entries are read together — that script checks the SHA is present, this one writes it when it is not. No upstream counterpart.

Upstream file, three additions and every one of them a list member: `dsh` appended to AGENT_ADAPTER_TYPES, the five Palantir roles (fda / core-swe / pre-sre / fdse / ds) appended to AGENT_ROLES, and `ontology_spec` appended to APPROVAL_TYPES. Appended rather than inserted, so no existing value changes meaning and no stored row is affected. They cannot live in our own tree because these are the shared unions the server, the clients and the adapters all compile against: a fork-local copy would let the two sides disagree about what a valid role or approval type is.

The fork's build surface: POST /build/start (the five-step issue chain), POST /build/spec/start (plan an ontology model and validate it against the plugin), GET /build/spec/:specId, and POST /build/spec/:specId/instantiate, which refuses unless the linked `ontology_spec` approval is approved and then calls the plugin's import-document through the provisioner. No upstream counterpart. It sits under server/src/routes/ because it mounts on the host router and needs host-side concerns — issues, approvals, the provisioner — that a plugin route cannot reach.

The five-step build chain (BUILD_TRIGGER_PATTERN, BUILD_STEP_KINDS, the per-step agent types) plus the ontology domain trigger, and `dispatchBuildStep`, which the spec decomposition reuses rather than re-implementing. No upstream counterpart. A host service rather than plugin code because it creates issues and paces dispatch through the host's own machinery.

Spawns the operator's local `hermes` CLI one-shot to plan a build or an ontology spec. No upstream counterpart. It has to sit in the host's service tree because the prompt it sends is assembled from host context (company id, API url, task markdown) and what comes back is a host-side plan — the plugin never spawns a process.

The host's side of the one sanctioned write path into the ontology plugin: it resolves the plugin through the registry and calls its validate-document and import-document routes in-process instead of writing the plugin's namespace itself. No upstream counterpart. It cannot live in the plugin because the authorization is the host's — the caller has already passed assertCompanyAccess, and the actor forwarded is the request's own rather than an identity this module invents.

Tests for the spec workflow's normalization: the document survives byte-identically to what the planner wrote (including the identifier flag the plugin validator requires, and enum/format/unit on properties), and a malformed or contradictory wrapper is refused rather than half-read — no object types, a missing phase, a phase named twice, an unknown phase — while a phase referring to an undeclared object type is dropped without failing the whole spec. No upstream counterpart.
Default Palantir 5 roles (FDA/Core-SWE/PRE-SRE/FDSE/DS) to Claude Code and Hermes adapters with self-healing rather than empty process adapter.
